column1: # 16장 말투 지시. 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).

column2: Wednesday night at home. Montse, Yuna's landlady in her seventies, appears dressed up in a blue dress and announces a night out on the Paral·lel, the old theatre avenue where she was young. Yuna doesn't know the place. Vale, an Argentine lodger, says "¡Dale!", Argentine for "let's go". Light and warm.
a plan already made, pleased with herself
explaining, then softer and nostalgic at "Allí fui joven"
surprised, then all in; "Dale" is Argentine for "let's go"

The Paral·lel at night. In front of El Molino, a cabaret theatre with a red windmill, Montse remembers coming there at twenty, in Franco's time, when people laughed at everything there. Then she reveals she once brought Sun-rye, Yuna's grandmother, in 1978. Yuna is struck to picture her grandmother young. Nostalgic, then a quiet ache.
honestly puzzled, a young person's question
plain and a little serious, then fond at the end
suddenly, quietly, still looking at the windmill
a warm memory; fond and amused at the end

A busy pintxos bar in Poble Sec. Vale explains how pintxos work using Argentine verb forms (comés, querés, pagás). Marc, a reserved locksmith, joins them. While Vale is away, Montse quietly tells Yuna and Marc a secret: Sun-rye left Barcelona for her little daughter's sake, and Martí never asked her to stay; he only made her a clock. Noisy bar, a hushed circle of three.
explaining like an old hand, Argentine forms

column1: Os voy a contar una cosa.
Sun-rye no se fue por su marido.
column2: a confession kept for years, quiet and unhurried
quiet and firm; stress the repeated "Nunca"

A taxi home late at night. Montse dozes in the front seat, then wakes just before they arrive and, in a very small voice, tells Yuna that the Tibidabo photographer's son sells old photos at the Sant Antoni market on Sundays. Yuna is left at the door with a new lead. Sleepy, hushed.
